{{for|Minkowski space-time|Minkowski space}}

In [[mathematics]], specifically the field of [[algebraic number theory]], a '''Minkowski space''' is a [[Euclidean space]] associated with an [[algebraic number field]].<ref>{{harvnb|Neukirch|1999|loc=[https://books.google.com/books?id=hS3qCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA28 p. 28]}}</ref>

If ''K'' is a number field of [[Degree of a number field|degree]] ''d'' then there are ''d'' distinct embeddings of ''K'' into '''C'''.   We let ''K''<sub>'''C'''</sub> be the image of ''K'' in the product '''C'''<sup>''d''</sup>, considered as equipped with the usual [[Hermitian inner product]].  If ''c'' denotes [[complex conjugation]], let ''K''<sub>'''R'''</sub> denote the subspace of ''K''<sub>'''C'''</sub> fixed by ''c'', equipped with a [[scalar product]].  This is the Minkowski space of ''K''.
